1	#!/bin/sh
2	# Exercise enable, lifecycle hooks, checkpoint capture and Brain setup in a
3	# scratch repository. Transcripts and distillation are scripted; no model is called.
4	# The real CLI and hooks run with sandboxed home/config/data/state roots and daemon
5	# registration disabled. Teardown compares service and config path listings.
6	#
7	# Environment:
8	#   DEMO_DIR=<path>          put the sandbox somewhere else (default: .demo-agent-session/)
9	#   DEMO_KEEP=1              keep the sandbox after the run (leak checks still run)
10	#   ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR=<path>  an entire-graph checkout, for the semantic component
11	#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=<path>  use this entire-brain binary instead of building one
12	set -eu
13	
14	is_brain_checkout() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -d "$1/cmd/entire-brain" ] && [ -f "$1/go.mod" ]; }
15	
16	script_path=$0
17	case $script_path in
18	*/*) ;;
19	*) script_path=$(command -v -- "$script_path" 2>/dev/null || printf './%s' "$script_path") ;;
20	esac
21	hops=0
22	while [ -L "$script_path" ] && [ "$hops" -lt 40 ]; do
23		link=$(readlink -- "$script_path")
24		case $link in
25		/*) script_path=$link ;;
26		*) script_path=$(dirname -- "$script_path")/$link ;;
27		esac
28		hops=$((hops + 1))
29	done
30	script_dir=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$script_path")" && pwd)
31	repo_root=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
32	if ! is_brain_checkout "$repo_root"; then
33		top=$(git -C "$script_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)
34		[ -n "$top" ] && is_brain_checkout "$top" && repo_root=$top
35	fi
36	
37	demo_dir=${DEMO_DIR:-"$repo_root/.demo-agent-session"}
38	keep=${DEMO_KEEP:-}
39	daemon_name=entire-brain-agent-demo
40	
41	# The scratch repo needs a github-shaped remote or entire-brain and entire-graph
42	# reduce it to different repo keys and the semantic snapshot is rejected. See
43	# scripts/demo-setup.sh for the derivation. Nothing is fetched from it, and the
44	# host CLI's inability to reach it is itself part of what this demo exercises.
45	demo_remote=https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain-agent-demo.git
46	
47	say() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
48	note() { printf '   %s\n' "$1"; }
49	die() { printf 'demo-agent-session: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }
50	
51	# fail is for a broken SEAM, not a broken environment: it means the chain this
52	# script exists to prove came apart, so it says which link and stops.
53	fail() {
54		printf '\n\033[1;31mSEAM BROKEN: %s\033[0m\n' "$1" >&2
55		exit 1
56	}
57	
58	command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'git is required'
59	is_brain_checkout "$repo_root" ||
60		die "this script must live in an entire-brain checkout; resolved $repo_root from $0, which has no cmd/entire-brain"
61	# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # literal backticks, prose not expansion
62	command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
63		die 'the parent `entire` CLI is required -- it is the thing under test here, not a helper. Install it from https://github.com/entireio/cli, then re-run'
64	
65	entire_bin=$(command -v entire)
66	brain_bin=${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-}
67	[ -n "$brain_bin" ] || command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
68		die 'a Go toolchain is required to build the branch binary, or set ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN to one you already have'
69	
70	if [ ! -t 1 ]; then
71		note 'stdout is not a terminal: setup renders its degraded plain fallback.'
72		note 'That is fine here -- this script proves the loop, not the repaints.'
73	fi
74	
75	# Only a directory created by this invocation may be cleaned up below.
76	if [ -e "$demo_dir" ] || [ -L "$demo_dir" ]; then
77		die "sandbox path already exists; refusing to overwrite it: $demo_dir"
78	fi
79	mkdir -- "$demo_dir" || die "could not create fresh sandbox: $demo_dir"
80	demo_dir=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$demo_dir" && pwd)
81	
82	sandbox_home="$demo_dir/home"
83	demo_repo="$demo_dir/repo"
84	stub_bin="$demo_dir/bin"
85	transcripts="$sandbox_home/transcripts"
86	mkdir -p "$sandbox_home" "$stub_bin" "$transcripts"
87	
88	sandbox_processes() {
89		ps -axo pid=,comm=,args= | awk -v root="$demo_dir" '$2 ~ /(^|\/)entire-brain$/ && index($0, root) { print $1 }'
90	}
91	
92	cleanup() {
93		status=$?
94		trap - EXIT INT TERM
95		# Stop only brain processes whose executable/arguments identify this sandbox.
96		pids=$(sandbox_processes)
97		if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
98			for pid in $pids; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done
99			attempts=0
100			while [ "$attempts" -lt 5 ] && [ -n "$(sandbox_processes)" ]; do
101				sleep 1
102				attempts=$((attempts + 1))
103			done
104			pids=$(sandbox_processes)
105			for pid in $pids; do kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done
106		fi
107		if [ -n "$(sandbox_processes)" ]; then
108			printf 'sandbox process still running; preserving %s\n' "$demo_dir" >&2
109			status=1
110		elif [ -z "$keep" ]; then
111			rm -rf "$demo_dir" || status=1
112		fi
113		exit "$status"
114	}
115	trap cleanup EXIT
116	trap 'exit 130' INT
117	trap 'exit 143' TERM
118	
119	# ------------------------------------------------------------ before snapshot
120	
121	service_state() {
122		if command -v launchctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
123			launchctl list 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}' | grep -i 'io\.entire\.' || true
124		fi
125		if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
126			systemctl --user list-unit-files --no-legend 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | grep -i 'entire' || true
127		fi
128		for dir in "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents" "$HOME/.config/systemd/user"; do
129			[ -d "$dir" ] || continue
130			find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*entire*' -exec basename {} \; 2>/dev/null || true
131		done
132	}
133	service_state | sort >"$demo_dir/services.before"
134	
135	real_config_dir=${ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR:-"${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/entire"}
136	real_config_state() { [ -d "$real_config_dir" ] && (cd "$real_config_dir" && find . | sort) || true; }
137	real_config_state >"$demo_dir/entire-config.before"
138	
139	# -------------------------------------------------------------- the sandbox
140	#
141	# `env -i` is deliberate: an inherited variable is exactly how a "sandboxed" run
142	# ends up writing to a real store. ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR is the one this script adds
143	# over demo-setup.sh's list -- `entire enable` writes login contexts there, and
144	# it is NOT derived from HOME on every platform.
145	#
146	# ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file keeps the CLI off the login keychain. It never logs in
147	# here (nothing in this demo needs an account) but a keychain prompt in the
148	# middle of a demo is its own kind of failure.
149	#
150	# PAGER/GIT_PAGER=cat is that same rule applied to OUTPUT, and it is not
151	# optional. TERM is set below, so under a captured pty --
152	#   script -q run.log ./scripts/demo-agent-session.sh
153	# -- stdout IS a terminal, and `entire checkpoint list` pages anything taller
154	# than the window through $PAGER (cmd/entire/cli/explain.go: outputWithPager ->
155	# buildPagerCmd, which reads PAGER and falls back to `less`). `less` then sits
156	# on "Press RETURN to continue" and the demo hangs forever, mid-run, with no
157	# further output. `cat` is honoured by that same lookup, so setting it here
158	# covers every child and grandchild in one place -- every `entire` verb, every
159	# `entire-brain` verb, and the `entire` binary entire-brain itself shells out
160	# to -- rather than a --no-pager flag bolted onto whichever command happens to
161	# page today.
162	#
163	# GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is the INPUT half of the same rule: a git child that
164	# wants a username or password must fail fast instead of blocking on the pty.
165	# The `entire` CLI already sets it on its own remote calls (internal/remote/
166	# git.go, disableTerminalPrompt); this extends the guarantee to every other git
167	# child the sandbox may start.
168	
169	sandbox() {
170		dir=$1
171		shift
172		(cd "$dir" && env -i \
173			PATH="$stub_bin:$(dirname -- "$entire_bin"):${PATH:-/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin}" \
174			TERM="${TERM:-xterm-256color}" \
175			LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" \
176			PAGER=cat \
177			GIT_PAGER=cat \
178			GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
179			GOMAXPROCS=4 \
180			HOME="$sandbox_home" \
181			XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$sandbox_home/.config" \
182			XDG_DATA_HOME="$sandbox_home/.local/share" \
183			XDG_STATE_HOME="$sandbox_home/.local/state" \
184			XDG_CACHE_HOME="$sandbox_home/.cache" \
185			ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$sandbox_home/.config/entire" \
186			ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file \
187			ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/config" \
188			ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/data" \
189			ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/state" \
190			ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/cache" \
191			ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR="$sandbox_home/daemon" \
192			ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1 \
193			"$@")
194	}
195	
196	brain() {
197		dir=$1
198		shift
199		sandbox "$dir" nice -n 10 "$brain_bin" "$@"
200	}
201	
202	# run_step prints the command, runs it, prints its exit code, and returns it.
203	# A demo whose steps have invisible exit codes is a demo that can be green while
204	# a step failed.
205	run_step() {
206		label=$1
207		shift
208		printf '   $ %s\n' "$label"
209		set +e
210		"$@"
211		step_status=$?
212		set -e
213		printf '   [exit %s]\n' "$step_status"
214		return $step_status
215	}
216	
217	# ----------------------------------------------------------------- 1. build
218	
219	say "1/9  build entire-brain"
220	if [ -n "$brain_bin" ]; then
221		[ -x "$brain_bin" ] || die "ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=$brain_bin is not executable"
222		note "using $brain_bin (ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN)"
223	else
224		brain_bin="$demo_dir/entire-brain"
225		(cd "$repo_root" && CGO_ENABLED="${CGO_ENABLED:-0}" GOMAXPROCS=4 nice -n 10 go build -p 2 -trimpath -o "$brain_bin" ./cmd/entire-brain)
226		note "$brain_bin"
227	fi
228	note "entire: $entire_bin ($("$entire_bin" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1))"
229	
230	# --------------------------------------------------------- 2. the repository
231	
232	say "2/9  a scratch repository with real content and real history"
233	
234	git init -q -b main "$demo_repo"
235	git -C "$demo_repo" config user.name 'Demo Runner'
236	git -C "$demo_repo" config user.email 'demo@example.invalid'
237	git -C "$demo_repo" config commit.gpgsign false
238	git -C "$demo_repo" remote add origin "$demo_remote"
239	
240	mkdir -p "$demo_repo/greet"
241	cat >"$demo_repo/go.mod" <<'GOMOD'
242	module example.com/demo
243	
244	go 1.22
245	GOMOD
246	cat >"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
247	// Package greet formats greetings.
248	package greet
249	
250	// Greet returns a greeting for name.
251	func Greet(name string) string {
252		return "hello " + name
253	}
254	SRC
255	cat >"$demo_repo/main.go" <<'SRC'
256	package main
257	
258	import (
259		"fmt"
260	
261		"example.com/demo/greet"
262	)
263	
264	func main() { fmt.Println(greet.Greet("world")) }
265	SRC
266	cat >"$demo_repo/README.md" <<'DOC'
267	# demo
268	
269	A tiny module used to demonstrate the Entire brain over a real agent session.
270	DOC
271	git -C "$demo_repo" add -A
272	git -C "$demo_repo" commit -qm 'feat: a greeting package'
273	note "$(git -C "$demo_repo" rev-list --count HEAD) commit, $(git -C "$demo_repo" ls-files | wc -l | tr -d ' ') tracked files, remote $demo_remote"
274	
275	# ------------------------------------------------------------ 3. entire enable
276	
277	say "3/9  entire enable  (installs git hooks + the agent's session hooks)"
278	note 'non-interactive because --agent is passed; it needs no login and no network'
279	run_step "entire enable --agent claude-code" sandbox "$demo_repo" entire enable --agent claude-code ||
280		fail "entire enable failed -- nothing downstream can work without it"
281	
282	[ -f "$demo_repo/.entire/settings.json" ] ||
283		fail "entire enable reported success but wrote no .entire/settings.json"
284	hook_settings="$demo_repo/.claude/settings.json"
285	[ -f "$hook_settings" ] ||
286		fail "entire enable reported success but wrote no .claude/settings.json, so no session-end hook exists"
287	grep -q 'hooks claude-code session-end' "$hook_settings" ||
288		fail "the settings entire enable wrote carry no session-end hook: $hook_settings"
289	note "session-end hook: $(grep -o 'entire hooks claude-code session-end' "$hook_settings" | head -n 1)"
290	note "checkpoint backend: $(sed -n 's/.*"type": *"\([a-z-]*\)".*/\1/p' "$demo_repo/.entire/settings.json" | head -n 1)"
291	
292	# `entire enable` writes those two directories and does NOT commit them, so the
293	# very next `entire-brain setup` finds a dirty worktree and refuses to seed or
294	# index it -- naming --worktree, a flag setup does not accept. That is a real
295	# first-run trap and the reason `setup` now carries a remedy for it; the honest
296	# fix for a user is the one applied here, because both files are project
297	# configuration that belongs in the repository anyway.
298	say "4/9  commit what enable wrote"
299	note 'setup refuses to index an uncommitted tree; enable leaves one behind'
300	# Through sandbox(), not bare `sh -c`. From here on this repository has the git
301	# hooks `entire enable` installed, so EVERY commit below runs `entire` -- and an
302	# unsandboxed commit would run it against the developer's real HOME and
303	# ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR, and would stop on the prepare-commit-msg hook's
304	# "Link this commit to session context? [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways" question. That
305	# question is asked on /dev/tty, not stdin, so redirecting input cannot answer
306	# it and the demo blocks forever on a human's terminal. sandbox() sets
307	# GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, which the CLI treats as "the caller cannot answer
308	# prompts" (cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go, isAgentSubprocessEnv) and
309	# auto-links instead of asking -- the same default the prompt itself carries.
310	run_step "stage and commit Entire configuration" \
311		sandbox "$demo_repo" sh -c "git add .entire .claude && git commit -qm 'chore: enable Entire session capture'" ||
312		fail "could not commit the files entire enable wrote"
313	
314	# ------------------------------------------------------- 5. the agent session
315	
316	say "5/9  an agent session, driven through the host CLI's own hook verbs"
317	note 'the model is substituted (this script writes the transcript); every hook,'
318	note 'the session state machine and the checkpoint writer are the real ones.'
319	
320	session_id=7f3a1c20-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1
321	transcript="$transcripts/$session_id.jsonl"
322	
323	hook() {
324		verb=$1
325		payload=$2
326		printf '%s' "$payload" | sandbox "$demo_repo" entire hooks claude-code "$verb"
327	}
328	
329	cat >"$transcript" <<JSONL
330	{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Greet(\"\") returns \"hello \" with a dangling space. Make an empty name greet \"there\" instead."},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:00.000Z"}
331	{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"demo-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll guard the empty name inside Greet rather than at the call sites."}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:05.000Z"}
332	JSONL
333	
334	run_step "entire hooks claude-code session-start" \
335		hook session-start "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"demo-substituted-model\",\"cwd\":\"$demo_repo\"}" ||
336		fail "the session-start hook failed"
337	
338	run_step "entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit" \
339		hook user-prompt-submit "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"prompt\":\"Make an empty name greet \\\"there\\\".\"}" ||
340		fail "the user-prompt-submit hook failed"
341	
342	# The edit an agent would have made, and the transcript entries recording it in
343	# Claude Code's own shape -- this is what the exporter later reads back.
344	cat >"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
345	// Package greet formats greetings.
346	package greet
347	
348	// Greet returns a greeting for name. An empty name greets "there" rather than
349	// producing a dangling "hello ", so no caller has to check first.
350	func Greet(name string) string {
351		if name == "" {
352			return "hello there"
353		}
354		return "hello " + name
355	}
356	SRC
357	cat >>"$transcript" <<JSONL
358	{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"demo-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"tu_1","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go","old_string":"return \"hello \" + name","new_string":"if name == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"hello there\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"hello \" + name"}}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:10.000Z"}
359	{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu_1","content":"The file has been updated."}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:11.000Z"}
360	{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"demo-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The empty-name guard lives inside Greet rather than at each call site, so no caller has to repeat the check."}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:12.000Z"}
361	JSONL
362	
363	run_step "entire hooks claude-code stop" \
364		hook stop "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"demo-substituted-model\"}" ||
365		fail "the stop hook failed"
366	
367	# The PERSISTENT checkpoint is written by the post-commit git hook `entire
368	# enable` installed, not by session-end: `entire checkpoint` has no verb that
369	# creates one (it is list/explain/tokens/search only). Committing is therefore
370	# part of the loop, not a tidy-up after it.
371	say "6/9  commit the session's work  (the post-commit hook writes the checkpoint)"
372	run_step "stage and commit the session work" \
373		sandbox "$demo_repo" sh -c "git add -A && git commit -qm 'fix(greet): greet \"there\" for an empty name'" ||
374		fail "the commit failed, so no post-commit hook ran"
375	
376	run_step "entire hooks claude-code session-end" \
377		hook session-end "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"demo-substituted-model\",\"reason\":\"clear\"}" ||
378		fail "the session-end hook failed"
379	
380	checkpoint_refs=$(git -C "$demo_repo" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/entire/checkpoints/' 'refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/')
381	[ -n "$checkpoint_refs" ] ||
382		fail "the session ended and NO checkpoint ref was written -- this is the seam a synthesised ref hides"
383	printf '%s\n' "$checkpoint_refs" | sed -e 's/^/   ref  /'
384	
385	# The two warning lines this step prints are TRUE, and they are left in
386	# deliberately. `entire enable` writes no checkpoint_remote, so the CLI falls
387	# back to `origin` for remote checkpoint discovery (cmd/entire/cli/
388	# git_operations.go, listCheckpointRefsOnRemote) -- and this demo's origin is
389	# the deliberately unreachable github.com URL above, which exists only so that
390	# entire-brain and entire-graph derive the same repo key from `git remote
391	# get-url origin`. Redirecting the warning away would hide the identical
392	# message in a real run, where an unreachable checkpoint remote is exactly the
393	# thing a user needs told; writing a checkpoint_remote into .entire/settings.json
394	# to make the CLI skip discovery would misrepresent what `entire enable` wrote,
395	# which is the artifact this script asserts on two steps above. So it is
396	# narrated instead of silenced.
397	printf '\n'
398	note 'the two warnings below are expected and correct: origin is deliberately'
399	note 'unreachable here, so remote checkpoint discovery fails and the list falls'
400	note 'back to local refs -- which is all this demo ever wrote. A real repo with'
401	note 'a reachable remote gets its remote checkpoints merged in at this point.'
402	run_step "entire checkpoint list" sandbox "$demo_repo" entire checkpoint list ||
403		fail "entire cannot read back the checkpoint it just wrote"
404	
405	# -------------------------------------------------- 7. the semantic provider
406	#
407	# Optional here, unlike in demo-setup.sh: this demo is about the session seam,
408	# and requiring a second checkout to see it would be the same mistake. When the
409	# provider is absent setup reports the semantic component as failed and every
410	# other component still builds.
411	
412	if [ -n "${ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR:-}" ]; then
413		graph_root=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd) ||
414			die "ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR=$ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR does not exist"
415	else
416		graph_root=
417		for candidate in "$repo_root/../entire-graph" "$repo_root/../../entire-graph" "${HOME:-}/devenv/entire-graph"; do
418			[ -n "$candidate" ] || continue
419			resolved=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$candidate" 2>/dev/null && pwd) || continue
420			[ -d "$resolved/cmd/entire-graph" ] || continue
421			graph_root=$resolved
422			break
423		done
424	fi
425	
426	say "7/9  the semantic provider"
427	if [ -n "$graph_root" ] && command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
428		note "building entire-graph from $graph_root"
429		(cd "$graph_root" && GOMAXPROCS=4 nice -n 10 go build -p 2 -trimpath -o "$demo_dir/entire-graph" ./cmd/entire-graph)
430		run_step "entire plugin install entire-graph --force" \
431			sandbox "$demo_repo" entire plugin install "$demo_dir/entire-graph" --force ||
432			fail "the provider would not register inside the sandbox"
433	else
434		note 'no entire-graph checkout found (set ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR to use one).'
435		note 'setup will report the semantic component as failed; everything else is'
436		note 'unaffected, and the session loop this script exists to prove does not'
437		note 'depend on it.'
438	fi
439	
440	# ------------------------------------------------------------ 8. the brain
441	
442	say "8/9  entire-brain setup  (over a checkpoint the host CLI actually wrote)"
443	run_step "entire-brain setup --no-backfill ." \
444		brain "$demo_repo" setup --daemon-name "$daemon_name" --no-backfill . ||
445		fail "setup exited non-zero: no component built"
446	
447	# The assertion the whole script is for. `brief` and `status` can look healthy
448	# off the seed baseline alone, so the session count is checked at the source.
449	session_count=$(brain "$demo_repo" status --json 2>/dev/null | tr ',' '\n' | sed -n 's/.*"sessions": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -n 1)
450	case ${session_count:-0} in
451	'' | 0) fail "setup built a brain with ZERO sessions -- the checkpoint written above never reached it" ;;
452	esac
453	note "setup found $session_count real captured session(s)"
454	
455	say "9/9  distill and query"
456	note 'the distill agent is a stub shell script: it reads the transcript on stdin'
457	note 'and prints fixed fact lines. It never calls a model and spends no tokens.'
458	
459	cat >"$stub_bin/entire-brain-demo-agent" <<'STUB'
460	#!/bin/sh
461	# Demo stub agent. NEVER calls a model, NEVER spends a token.
462	set -eu
463	
464	for arg in "$@"; do
465		case $arg in
466		--version) printf 'entire-brain demo stub agent 1.0.0\n'; exit 0 ;;
467		esac
468	done
469	
470	input=$(cat 2>/dev/null || true)
471	
472	# The reconciler reuses the same agent with a different input shape.
473	case $input in
474	CANDIDATES*)
475		printf '%s\n' "$input" | awk '/^CANDIDATES$/ {seen=1; next} seen && /^[0-9]+/ {printf "%s new - 1.0\n", $1}'
476		exit 0
477		;;
478	esac
479	
480	# One fact, drawn from what the session actually decided. The path must sit
481	# under a shipped taxonomy category or the fact is dropped.
482	printf 'architecture\tarchitecture.boundaries.rationale\tThe empty-name guard lives inside Greet rather than at each call site, so no caller has to repeat the check.\n'
483	STUB
484	chmod +x "$stub_bin/entire-brain-demo-agent"
485	
486	run_step "entire-brain distill --agent command ." \
487		brain "$demo_repo" distill --agent command --agent-command "$stub_bin/entire-brain-demo-agent" . ||
488		fail "distillation of a real session failed"
489	
490	printf '\n'
491	run_step "entire-brain status" brain "$demo_repo" status || fail "status failed"
492	printf '\n'
493	run_step "entire-brain overview" brain "$demo_repo" overview || fail "overview failed"
494	
495	printf '\n'
496	brief_task='change how Greet handles an empty name'
497	brief_out=$(brain "$demo_repo" brief "$brief_task" 2>&1) || fail "brief failed"
498	printf '   $ entire-brain brief "%s"\n' "$brief_task"
499	printf '%s\n' "$brief_out" | sed -e 's/^/   /'
500	
501	# A brief that answers off the seed baseline alone would prove nothing, so both
502	# session-derived lines are required: the exported transcript, and the fact
503	# distilled from it.
504	printf '%s' "$brief_out" | grep -q "$session_id" ||
505		fail "brief drew nothing from the session -- it never reached the history layer"
506	printf '%s' "$brief_out" | grep -q 'architecture.boundaries.rationale' ||
507		fail "brief drew no distilled fact from the session"
508	note 'both lines above came from the session captured in step 5.'
509	
510	# ------------------------------------------------------------- the leak checks
511	
512	say "teardown and leak checks"
513	
514	leaked=0
515	service_state | sort >"$demo_dir/services.after"
516	if ! diff -u "$demo_dir/services.before" "$demo_dir/services.after" >"$demo_dir/services.diff" 2>&1; then
517		printf '   LEAK  the machine gained or lost a service:\n'
518		cat "$demo_dir/services.diff"
519		leaked=1
520	else
521		printf '   ok    service-name and unit-file listings match the pre-run snapshot\n'
522	fi
523	
524	if command -v launchctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
525		found=$(launchctl list 2>/dev/null | grep -i "$daemon_name" || true)
526		if [ -n "$found" ]; then
527			printf '   LEAK  a demo job is registered with launchd:\n%s\n' "$found"
528			leaked=1
529		else
530			printf '   ok    launchctl list has no %s job\n' "$daemon_name"
531		fi
532	else
533		printf '   skip  launchctl (not present)\n'
534	fi
535	
536	if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
537		found=$(systemctl --user list-units --all --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -i "$daemon_name" || true)
538		if [ -n "$found" ]; then
539			printf '   LEAK  a demo unit is registered with systemd:\n%s\n' "$found"
540			leaked=1
541		else
542			printf '   ok    systemctl --user has no %s unit\n' "$daemon_name"
543		fi
544	else
545		printf '   skip  systemctl (not present)\n'
546	fi
547	
548	# `entire enable` is the reason this check exists: it is the one step here that
549	# writes outside the repository, and if ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR were not redirected it
550	# would write login contexts into the developer's real store.
551	real_config_state >"$demo_dir/entire-config.after"
552	if diff -u "$demo_dir/entire-config.before" "$demo_dir/entire-config.after" >"$demo_dir/entire-config.diff" 2>&1; then
553		printf '   ok    %s path listing is unchanged\n' "$real_config_dir"
554	else
555		printf '   LEAK  the real Entire config store changed:\n'
556		cat "$demo_dir/entire-config.diff"
557		leaked=1
558	fi
559	
560	if [ -f "$sandbox_home/.config/entire/contexts.json.lock" ] || [ -d "$sandbox_home/.config/entire" ]; then
561		printf '   ok    the Entire CLI wrote its state inside the sandbox\n'
562	else
563		printf '   LEAK  the Entire CLI wrote no state inside the sandbox -- where did it go?\n'
564		leaked=1
565	fi
566	
567	if [ -n "$keep" ]; then
568		printf '\n   sandbox kept at %s\n' "$demo_dir"
569	fi
570	
571	printf '\n'
572	[ "$leaked" -eq 0 ] || die 'the demo leaked state outside its sandbox (see LEAK lines above)'
573	printf 'demo-agent-session: OK -- enable, a session, its hooks, a real checkpoint,\n'
574	printf 'setup, distill and brief all ran end to end. Zero tokens were spent; the\n'
575	printf 'only substituted component was the model that would have written the\n'
576	printf 'transcript.\n'

#!/bin/sh
# Exercise enable, lifecycle hooks, checkpoint capture and Brain setup in a
# scratch repository. Transcripts and distillation are scripted; no model is called.
# The real CLI and hooks run with sandboxed home/config/data/state roots and daemon
# registration disabled. Teardown compares service and config path listings.
#
# Environment:
#   DEMO_DIR=<path>          put the sandbox somewhere else (default: .demo-agent-session/)
#   DEMO_KEEP=1              keep the sandbox after the run (leak checks still run)
#   ENTIRE_GRAPH_DIR=<path>  an entire-graph checkout, for the semantic component
#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=<path>  use this entire-brain binary instead of building one
set -eu

is_brain_checkout() { [ -n "${1:-}" ] && [ -d "$1/cmd/entire-brain" ] && [ -f "$1/go.mod" ]; }

script_path=$0
case $script_path in
*/*) ;;
*) script_path=$(command -v -- "$script_path" 2>/dev/null || printf './%s' "$script_path") ;;
esac
hops=0
while [ -L "$script_path" ] && [ "$hops" -lt 40 ]; do
	link=$(readlink -- "$script_path")
	case $link in
	/*) script_path=$link ;;
	*) script_path=$(dirname -- "$script_path")/$link ;;
	esac
	hops=$((hops + 1))
done
script_dir=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$(dirname -- "$script_path")" && pwd)
repo_root=$(CDPATH='' cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
if ! is_brain_checkout "$repo_root"; then
	top=$(git -C "$script_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)
	[ -n "$top" ] && is_brain_checkout "$top" && repo_root=$top
fi

demo_dir=${DEMO_DIR:-"$repo_root/.demo-agent-session"}
keep=${DEMO_KEEP:-}
daemon_name=entire-brain-agent-demo

# The scratch repo needs a github-shaped remote or entire-brain and entire-graph
# reduce it to different repo keys and the semantic snapshot is rejected. See
# scripts/demo-setup.sh for the derivation. Nothing is fetched from it, and the
# host CLI's inability to reach it is itself part of what this demo exercises.
demo_remote=https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain-agent-demo.git

say() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
note() { printf '   %s\n' "$1"; }
die() { printf 'demo-agent-session: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit 1; }

# fail is for a broken SEAM, not a broken environment: it means the chain this
# script exists to prove came apart, so it says which link and stops.
fail() {
	printf '\n\033[1;31mSEAM BROKEN: %s\033[0m\n' "$1" >&2
	exit 1
}

command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 'git is required'
is_brain_checkout "$repo_root" ||
	die "this script must live in an entire-brain checkout; resolved $repo_root from $0, which has no cmd/entire-brain"
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # literal backticks, prose not expansion
command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
	die 'the parent `entire` CLI is required -- it is the thing under test here, not a helper. Install it from https://github.com/entireio/cli, then re-run'

entire_bin=$(command -v entire)
brain_bin=${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-}
[ -n "$brain_bin" ] || command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
	die 'a Go toolchain is required to build the branch binary, or set ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN to one you already have'

if [ ! -t 1 ]; then
	note 'stdout is not a terminal: setup renders its degraded plain fallback.'
	note 'That is fine here -- this script proves the loop, not the repaints.'

	status=$?

		while [ "$attempts" -lt 5 ] && [ -n "$(sandbox_processes)" ]; do
			sleep 1
			attempts=$((attempts + 1))
		done
		pids=$(sandbox_processes)
		for pid in $pids; do kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done

		printf 'sandbox process still running; preserving %s\n' "$demo_dir" >&2

real_config_dir=${ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR:-"${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/entire"}

# -------------------------------------------------------------- the sandbox
#
# `env -i` is deliberate: an inherited variable is exactly how a "sandboxed" run
# ends up writing to a real store. ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR is the one this script adds
# over demo-setup.sh's list -- `entire enable` writes login contexts there, and
# it is NOT derived from HOME on every platform.
#
# ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file keeps the CLI off the login keychain. It never logs in
# here (nothing in this demo needs an account) but a keychain prompt in the
# middle of a demo is its own kind of failure.
#
# PAGER/GIT_PAGER=cat is that same rule applied to OUTPUT, and it is not
# optional. TERM is set below, so under a captured pty --
#   script -q run.log ./scripts/demo-agent-session.sh
# -- stdout IS a terminal, and `entire checkpoint list` pages anything taller
# than the window through $PAGER (cmd/entire/cli/explain.go: outputWithPager ->
# buildPagerCmd, which reads PAGER and falls back to `less`). `less` then sits
# on "Press RETURN to continue" and the demo hangs forever, mid-run, with no
# further output. `cat` is honoured by that same lookup, so setting it here
# covers every child and grandchild in one place -- every `entire` verb, every
# `entire-brain` verb, and the `entire` binary entire-brain itself shells out
# to -- rather than a --no-pager flag bolted onto whichever command happens to
# page today.
#
# GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is the INPUT half of the same rule: a git child that
# wants a username or password must fail fast instead of blocking on the pty.
# The `entire` CLI already sets it on its own remote calls (internal/remote/
# git.go, disableTerminalPrompt); this extends the guarantee to every other git
# child the sandbox may start.

sandbox() {
	dir=$1
	shift
	(cd "$dir" && env -i \
		PATH="$stub_bin:$(dirname -- "$entire_bin"):${PATH:-/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin}" \
		TERM="${TERM:-xterm-256color}" \
		LANG="${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}" \
		PAGER=cat \
		GIT_PAGER=cat \
		GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
		GOMAXPROCS=4 \
		HOME="$sandbox_home" \
		XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$sandbox_home/.config" \
		XDG_DATA_HOME="$sandbox_home/.local/share" \
		XDG_STATE_HOME="$sandbox_home/.local/state" \
		XDG_CACHE_HOME="$sandbox_home/.cache" \
		ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$sandbox_home/.config/entire" \
		ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file \
		ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/config" \
		ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/data" \
		ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/state" \
		ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$sandbox_home/plugin/cache" \
		ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR="$sandbox_home/daemon" \
		ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1 \
		"$@")
}

brain() {
	dir=$1
	shift
	sandbox "$dir" nice -n 10 "$brain_bin" "$@"
}

# run_step prints the command, runs it, prints its exit code, and returns it.
# A demo whose steps have invisible exit codes is a demo that can be green while
# a step failed.
run_step() {
	label=$1
	shift
	printf '   $ %s\n' "$label"
	set +e
	"$@"
	step_status=$?
	set -e
	printf '   [exit %s]\n' "$step_status"
	return $step_status
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- 1. build

say "1/9  build entire-brain"
if [ -n "$brain_bin" ]; then
	[ -x "$brain_bin" ] || die "ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=$brain_bin is not executable"
	note "using $brain_bin (ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN)"
else
	brain_bin="$demo_dir/entire-brain"
	(cd "$repo_root" && CGO_ENABLED="${CGO_ENABLED:-0}" GOMAXPROCS=4 nice -n 10 go build -p 2 -trimpath -o "$brain_bin" ./cmd/entire-brain)

say "2/9  a scratch repository with real content and real history"

git init -q -b main "$demo_repo"
git -C "$demo_repo" config user.name 'Demo Runner'
git -C "$demo_repo" config user.email 'demo@example.invalid'
git -C "$demo_repo" config commit.gpgsign false
git -C "$demo_repo" remote add origin "$demo_remote"

mkdir -p "$demo_repo/greet"
cat >"$demo_repo/go.mod" <<'GOMOD'
module example.com/demo

go 1.22
GOMOD
cat >"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name.
func Greet(name string) string {
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
cat >"$demo_repo/main.go" <<'SRC'

	"fmt"

	"example.com/demo/greet"
)

SRC

# demo

A tiny module used to demonstrate the Entire brain over a real agent session.
DOC
git -C "$demo_repo" add -A
git -C "$demo_repo" commit -qm 'feat: a greeting package'
note "$(git -C "$demo_repo" rev-list --count HEAD) commit, $(git -C "$demo_repo" ls-files | wc -l | tr -d ' ') tracked files, remote $demo_remote"

note 'non-interactive because --agent is passed; it needs no login and no network'
run_step "entire enable --agent claude-code" sandbox "$demo_repo" entire enable --agent claude-code ||
	fail "entire enable failed -- nothing downstream can work without it"

[ -f "$demo_repo/.entire/settings.json" ] ||
	fail "entire enable reported success but wrote no .entire/settings.json"
hook_settings="$demo_repo/.claude/settings.json"
[ -f "$hook_settings" ] ||
	fail "entire enable reported success but wrote no .claude/settings.json, so no session-end hook exists"
grep -q 'hooks claude-code session-end' "$hook_settings" ||
	fail "the settings entire enable wrote carry no session-end hook: $hook_settings"
note "session-end hook: $(grep -o 'entire hooks claude-code session-end' "$hook_settings" | head -n 1)"
note "checkpoint backend: $(sed -n 's/.*"type": *"\([a-z-]*\)".*/\1/p' "$demo_repo/.entire/settings.json" | head -n 1)"

# very next `entire-brain setup` finds a dirty worktree and refuses to seed or
# index it -- naming --worktree, a flag setup does not accept. That is a real
# first-run trap and the reason `setup` now carries a remedy for it; the honest
# fix for a user is the one applied here, because both files are project
# configuration that belongs in the repository anyway.
say "4/9  commit what enable wrote"
note 'setup refuses to index an uncommitted tree; enable leaves one behind'
# Through sandbox(), not bare `sh -c`. From here on this repository has the git
# hooks `entire enable` installed, so EVERY commit below runs `entire` -- and an
# unsandboxed commit would run it against the developer's real HOME and
# ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR, and would stop on the prepare-commit-msg hook's

	sandbox "$demo_repo" sh -c "git add .entire .claude && git commit -qm 'chore: enable Entire session capture'" ||

note 'the session state machine and the checkpoint writer are the real ones.'

hook() {

cat >"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Greet(\"\") returns \"hello \" with a dangling space. Make an empty name greet \"there\" instead."},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:00.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"demo-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll guard the empty name inside Greet rather than at the call sites."}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:05.000Z"}
JSONL

run_step "entire hooks claude-code session-start" \

# The edit an agent would have made, and the transcript entries recording it in
# Claude Code's own shape -- this is what the exporter later reads back.
cat >"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name. An empty name greets "there" rather than
// producing a dangling "hello ", so no caller has to check first.
func Greet(name string) string {
	if name == "" {
		return "hello there"
	}
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
cat >>"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"demo-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"tu_1","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"$demo_repo/greet/greet.go","old_string":"return \"hello \" + name","new_string":"if name == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"hello there\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"hello \" + name"}}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:10.000Z"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu_1","content":"The file has been updated."}]},"timestamp":"2026-09-05T10:00:11.000Z"}

content.content:
connect binds this repository to its hosted brain: it records the repo id and
API base URL (non-secrets only — the host CLI's own login mints a fresh token
per sync), then runs one immediate sync so the first pull happens right away.

Running connect (or the onboarding flow) is the ONLY way a repository starts
syncing: by default memories stay local and background triggers never connect
a repo on their own. Placement resolves through the host CLI (entire repo
view); pass --repo-id and --api-url to bypass resolution — a non-default cell
or a staging target. Re-running connect re-joins after 'entire brain
disconnect'.

Usage:
  entire-brain connect [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string   Entire API base URL, https://
  -h, --help             help for connect
      --repo-id string   Hosted repo id (region-local ULID)

----
sync runs the factsync read-merge-CAS loop for the current branch: pull the
current memory-set head, keep-both merge this member's local memories into it,
and compare-and-swap the result back; retrying on a losing swap.

Backends (--memories-backend, or ENTIRE_BRAIN_FACTS_BACKEND):
  local-gitmeta  (default) a bare, on-disk git-meta store under the brain cache
                 (<cache>/brain/<repo-key>/gitmeta.git); fully local, no network,
                 entiredb, or Postgres. This is the default whether or not the
                 repo is connected: a plain sync never leaves the machine.
  http           the hosted entire-api FactSetStore; opt-in with
                 --memories-backend=http. Target resolves flag > env > connected
                 binding: --api-url/ENTIRE_API_URL, --repo-id/ENTIRE_REPO_ID,
                 --token/ENTIRE_API_TOKEN; on a connected repo the binding
                 supplies the target and the token is minted automatically.

Usage:
  entire-brain memories sync [flags]

Flags:
      --api-url string            Entire API base URL for the http backend, https:// (overrides ENTIRE_API_URL)
      --branch string             Branch to sync (default: current branch)
  -h, --help                      help for sync
      --json                      Emit the sync result as JSON
      --member string             Member identity stamped on cross-member proposals (default: git user.email)
      --memories-backend string   Memory-set backend: local-gitmeta (default) or http
      --repo-id string            Target repo id for the http backend (overrides ENTIRE_REPO_ID)
      --token string              Entire API bearer token for the http backend (overrides ENTIRE_API_TOKEN)

content.content:
Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph query --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]
  entire graph query [flags] "issue or concept"

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default query returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--verify-block off (or --omit-verify, or ENTIRE_GRAPH_VERIFY_BLOCK=off) removes the VERIFY block and nothing else: the test command and the run-once/fix/stop advice that rides with it. That advice would help an agent with no tool just as much, so it exists for fair A/B comparisons (both arms get it, or neither). JSON then omits verify_command and reports stats.verify_omitted. In agent format the freed bytes go to ranked results under the same --max-context-bytes, so off is a different selection, not the on payload with lines deleted.

--top-k caps normal results, including automatic related sites and covering tests, without changing retrieval strategy. Explicit --callee-hop may add called-helper results beyond that cap, under its existing byte-budget and ranked-source protections. --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence; alternatively supply one final argument
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Maximum normal results, including related/covering entries (--callee-hop may add helpers) (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --callee-hop              Add called-helper results beyond --top-k, subject to byte-budget and ranked-source protections
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded. Unset with --format agent: the smallest of 4096/8192/16384 that shows the top hit whole, else 24576 (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --verify-block on|off     off removes the VERIFY block (suggested test command plus its run/fix/stop advice) in every format; exists for fair A/B comparisons against an arm with no tool. Env: ENTIRE_GRAPH_VERIFY_BLOCK (default: on)
  --omit-verify             Shorthand for --verify-block off
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

Examples:
  entire graph query --repo . --format text "token refresh returns 401"
  entire graph query --repo . --query "token refresh returns 401" --format text --top-k 8
  entire graph query --repo . --query "csv export ordering" --profile full

content.content:
Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch

Usage:
  entire-brain recall <query> [flags]

Flags:
      --agent string                     Agent for --expand: auto, codex, claude-code, ollama, or command (default "auto")
      --agent-command stringArray        Agent command argv for --agent command
      --all                              Include superseded and retracted memories
      --branch string                    Branch to recall from (default: current branch)
      --eligible-before string           Restrict candidates to memories whose provenance is strictly before this RFC3339 cutoff
      --evidence                         Experimental: return original source spans using deterministic retrieval; no model call
      --evidence-bytes int               Maximum compact JSON bytes in the evidence array, including citations; enclosing metadata is separate (default 8192)
      --exclude-session-id stringArray   Exclude memories anchored to this session (repeatable)
      --expand                           Expand the query with agent-generated retrieval terms before ranking
  -h, --help                             help for recall
      --json                             Emit machine-readable JSON
      --k int                            Maximum memories to return, or candidate sessions with --evidence (1-128) (default 10)
      --kind string                      Restrict to one kind: decision|invariant|gotcha|preference|convention
      --locus string                     Restrict to memories about a code locus (a path or symbol, e.g. internal/cli/facts.go or factRecord)
      --model string                     Model for codex/claude-code/ollama expand calls
      --no-global                        Exclude global memories, recalling only this repository's
      --no-semantic                      Accepted for compatibility: semantic retrieval was removed, ranking is always BM25 lexical
      --read-only-semantic-cache         Accepted for compatibility: semantic vector caches no longer exist
      --scope string                     Restrict to 'local' (code/subsystem) or 'cross-cutting' (preferences/workflow) memories
      --session-dates string             JSON map of session IDs to provenance timestamps for --eligible-before

----
Summarize recorded sources, freshness, background activity, and live workspace state without scanning index contents. Use doctor for deep integrity checks.

Usage:
  entire-brain status [path] [flags]

Flags:
      --details          Include staged, unstaged, and untracked file classifications (does not audit index contents)
      --fail-on string   Return nonzero after emitting the report when the selected gate trips: release, unsafe, degraded, blind-spots, none (default "none")
  -h, --help             help for status
      --json             Emit machine-readable JSON
      --verbose          Print the full report (coverage, freshness axes, blind spots, live state) instead of the short summary

content.thinking:
I'm working out the backend flag choices for the sync commands — pinning the hosted HTTP backend explicitly for the upload leg since connected repos default is shifting away from gitmeta, and making sure local legs also pin their backend explicitly to avoid ambiguity.

That sync command should pull the remote head, merge local facts into it, and CAS it back, so it actually handles both push and pull in one call. Rather than asserting "visible remotely" directly in leg 6, I'll have leg 6 check the sync JSON result for the CAS swap acceptance, and let leg 7's pull on a fresh clone be the real proof of remote visibility, since an extra API read would add unverified assumptions.

For the distill step, I need to pick a cheap agent setup — checking whether claude or codex is actually on PATH, then choosing model/effort flags accordingly, since model aliases differ between the two agents and I want this to fail clearly if neither is available.

For the graph leg, I'm querying the committed tree for the greet function to confirm the symbol resolves correctly, then running the non-interactive enable step for claude-code, followed by verifying the checkpoint ref gets created under refs/entire/checkpoints.

Now thinking about sandboxing: since leg 6 needs real host auth and a real claude install, I can't use the env -i isolated approach from demo-agent-session.sh since that would break claude's credentials. Instead I should follow hosted-sync-smoke.sh's pattern — keep the host HOME/auth intact but redirect ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR per simulated machine to isolate brain state between them.

Running `entire enable` on a scratch repo should be safe since it just writes `.entire/.claude` locally, and setting GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 avoids any tty prompt issues during hook commits. For the daemon side, I need to figure out whether to set ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER for the smoke test similar to how the demo script handles it.

For the smoke test of the RC, I should actually use the installed `entire` binary and installed plugins rather than a built binary, calling `entire brain ...` from inside the scratch repo so the plugin registry resolves naturally and the exported ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR vars just redirect data and cache locations without needing full isolation.

Plugin registration lives in the host CLI config, which stays untouched, so redirecting plugin config/data dirs shouldn't hide registration. I also need a fake but unique github-shaped remote per run since `entire enable` expects that for brain/graph repo keys, matching what the demo does.

For fixtures, I can keep things minimal by embedding both the tiny session transcript and the tiny code repo inline via heredocs in the script rather than creating separate fixture files.

For the distill step, I need to run setup with no-backfill to pick up sessions from checkpoints, then distill on the scratch repo's main branch so recall later runs on the same branch. For the assertion, I'll check the distill --json output for a nonzero count of memories written rather than relying on a separate memories list command.

Since fact wording from a real model is unpredictable, I'll give the fixture transcript a distinctive but natural decision (like a fallback greeting of "there" for empty names) and then recall on related keywords, asserting the facts array is non-empty via BM25 matching rather than exact text. I also need the script to explicitly unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS to ensure egress isn't blocked.

For evidence output, I'll write a timestamped markdown file capturing version info and pass/fail per leg, redacting $HOME, and decide it should go to a configurable path like `.smoke-evidence/` rather than `.context/` since that's conductor-specific. I'm placing the script itself as a file task under `mise-tasks/release/` named `release:smoke`.

I need to make sure the script passes shellcheck since lint:shellcheck will run against it, so I'll use a clean bash shebang. I should also check whether oxfmt applies here given it's typically a JS formatter in what seems to be a Go repo, and I need to document the staging environment variables like ENTIRE_SMOKE_REPO_ID and ENTIRE_SMOKE_API_URL for the smoke test.

content.content:
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

Existing git hooks are kept: each is moved to <hook>.pre-entire and runs after
Entire's hook.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string        Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

  entire-brain refresh [command]

Available Commands:
  delta       Cheap short-term memory update: export new checkpoints and index only changed transcripts

  index       Build a local semantic brain index
  seed        Seed a brain from repository docs and code structure
  sessions    Export latest known transcript for each Entire session

Flags:
      --agent string    Agent synthesis mode for seed: auto, none, codex, claude-code, or command (default "auto")
      --force           Force a full refresh; overwrite explicit output when used with --output
  -h, --help            help for refresh
  -o, --output string   Output directory for the brain (default: persistent brain directory)
      --worktree        Refresh seed and docs from the current worktree

Use "entire-brain refresh [command] --help" for more information about a command.

input.description: Show brain setup flags

content.content:
setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (semantic index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by five
gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends (default no, and a run with no
terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

EXIT CODE: setup exits 0 whenever the brain is QUERYABLE, and queryable means
it can answer: at least one of the semantic index, the seed baseline or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and
"entire brain overview" read, so "entire brain setup && entire brain query ..." cannot proceed on a
brain that has nothing to answer from. A component that fails without costing
that (a doc index, an entity index, a stale semantic snapshot beside a seed
that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the
backfill, the workspace registration and the daemon install all still run;
"entire brain status" then shows that component as failed and "entire brain doctor" prints

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
#MISE description="Release smoke: full user journey on scratch repos (enable, capture, distill, recall, graph, hosted sync up/down)"
#
# A tripwire, not a test suite: one assert per leg, each fails loudly.
# Legs: 1 setup, 2 checkpoint capture, 3 distill, 4 recall, 5 graph query,
#        6 hosted upload (staging), 7 pull+merge on a second clone.
#
# The entire-brain binary under test is built from this checkout (the RC SHA);
# the host `entire` CLI and the entire-graph provider are the installed ones.
# Brain state is isolated per "machine" via ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR, like
# scripts/hosted-sync-smoke.sh; HOME and the host CLI's login stay real because
# legs 3 and 6 need the real coding agent and the real staging auth.
#
# Environment the runner must export (legs 6-7; never hardcode secrets):
#   REPO_ID       region-local repo ULID of a STAGING brainstore repo
#   API_URL       that repo's home-cell base URL, e.g. https://aws-us-west-2.api.partial.to/api/v1
#   AUTH_CONTEXT  optional saved `entire auth` login to mint the token from
#                 (e.g. us.auth.partial.to); default: the active context
#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN  optional prebuilt entire-brain binary (skips go build)
#
# Evidence: a timestamped pass/fail summary (with brain/graph/host versions)
# is written under .smoke-evidence/ with host paths redacted.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
evidence_dir=${SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR:-"$repo_root/.smoke-evidence"}
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
evidence="$evidence_dir/release-smoke-$stamp.md"

REPO_ID=${REPO_ID:?export REPO_ID (staging brainstore repo ULID) -- see header}
API_URL=${API_URL:?export API_URL (staging cell base URL) -- see header}

# Hosted sync fails closed under the egress kill switch; this suite exists to
# exercise egress, so both spellings must be unset.
unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY

command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: git is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v entire >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: the entire CLI is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: python3 is required" >&2; exit 1; }
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null && ! command -v codex >/dev/null; then
  echo "FATAL: leg 3 (distill) needs a coding agent on PATH (claude or codex)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ -n "${AUTH_CONTEXT:-}" ]; then
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token --context "$AUTH_CONTEXT")
else
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token)
fi
export ENTIRE_TOKEN

work=$(mktemp -d)
smoke_branch="smoke-$stamp"
scratch="$work/a"
clone_b="$work/b"

declare -a leg_names=(
  "1 setup: enable + brain setup healthy"
  "2 capture: commit writes a checkpoint"
  "3 distill: real agent writes >=1 fact"
  "4 recall: distilled fact comes back"
  "5 graph: fixture symbol resolves"
  "6 upload: hosted sync up, fact visible remotely"
  "7 pull: second clone pulls + merges the fact"
)
declare -a leg_status=(not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run)
current_leg=0

versions() {
  printf -- '- host CLI: %s\n' "$(entire version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
  printf -- '- entire-brain (under test): %s\n' "$("$brain_bin" version 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
  printf -- '- entire-graph: %s\n' "$(entire graph version --json 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
}

finalize() {
  status=$?
  trap - EXIT
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || [ "$current_leg" -eq 0 ] || leg_status[current_leg - 1]=FAIL
  mkdir -p "$evidence_dir"
  {
    echo "# release:smoke $stamp"
    echo
    echo "result: $([ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo PASS || echo "FAIL (exit $status)")"
    echo "rc sha: $(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse HEAD)"
    echo "staging repo: $REPO_ID @ $API_URL"
    echo
    versions
    echo
    for i in "${!leg_names[@]}"; do
      echo "- [${leg_status[$i]}] ${leg_names[$i]}"
    done
  } | sed -e "s|$work|\$WORK|g" -e "s|$HOME|~|g" >"$evidence"
  echo
  echo "evidence: $evidence"
  cat "$evidence"
  rm -rf "$work"
  exit "$status"
}
trap finalize EXIT

leg() {
  current_leg=$1
  printf '\n== leg %s: %s\n' "$1" "${leg_names[$1 - 1]#* }"
}
pass() { leg_status[current_leg - 1]=PASS; }
fail() {
  echo "SMOKE FAIL (leg $current_leg): $1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# machine <a|b> <workdir> <cmd...>: run a command against one isolated
# "machine" (its own plugin data/state/config/cache), real HOME and login.
# GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes the commit hooks auto-link instead of prompting.
machine() {
  local m=$1 dir=$2
  shift 2
  (cd "$dir" && env \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$work/$m/data" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$work/$m/state" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$work/$m/config" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$work/$m/cache" \
    ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1 \
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
    PAGER=cat GIT_PAGER=cat \
    "$@")
}

brain_a() { machine a "$scratch" env ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="$scratch" "$brain_bin" "$@"; }
brain_b() { machine b "$clone_b" env ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="$clone_b" "$brain_bin" "$@"; }

json_has_fact() { # json_has_fact <needle>: stdin JSON contains <needle> in any string value
  python3 -c '
import json, sys
needle = sys.argv[1]
def walk(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return needle in v
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return any(walk(x) for x in v.values())
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return any(walk(x) for x in v)
    return False
sys.exit(0 if walk(json.load(sys.stdin)) else 1)' "$1"
}

echo "== build entire-brain from this checkout"
brain_bin=${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-}
if [ -n "$brain_bin" ]; then
  [ -x "$brain_bin" ] || { echo "FATAL: ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=$brain_bin is not executable" >&2; exit 1; }
else
  command -v go >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: go is required to build entire-brain (or set ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN)" >&2; exit 1; }
  brain_bin="$work/entire-brain"
  (cd "$repo_root" && go build -o "$brain_bin" ./cmd/entire-brain)
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 1: setup
leg 1

# The remote must be github-shaped or entire-brain and entire-graph derive
# different repo keys (see scripts/demo-agent-session.sh). Never fetched.
git init -q -b main "$scratch"
git -C "$scratch" config user.name 'Release Smoke'
git -C "$scratch" config user.email 'release-smoke@example.invalid'
git -C "$scratch" config commit.gpgsign false
git -C "$scratch" remote add origin "https://github.com/entireio/release-smoke-$stamp.git"

mkdir -p "$scratch/greet"
cat >"$scratch/go.mod" <<'GOMOD'
module example.com/smoke

go 1.22
GOMOD
cat >"$scratch/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name.
func Greet(name string) string {
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
git -C "$scratch" add -A
git -C "$scratch" commit -qm 'feat: greeting package'
git -C "$scratch" checkout -qb "$smoke_branch"

machine a "$scratch" entire enable --agent claude-code
machine a "$scratch" sh -c "git add .entire .claude && git commit -qm 'chore: enable Entire'"
brain_a setup --no-backfill --no-daemon .
brain_a status --json --fail-on degraded >/dev/null ||
  fail "entire brain status reports a degraded brain right after setup"
pass

# -------------------------------------------------------------- leg 2: capture
leg 2

session_id=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')
transcript="$work/$session_id.jsonl"
hook() { # hook <verb> <payload-json>
  printf '%s' "$2" | machine a "$scratch" entire hooks claude-code "$1"
}

# The fixture session: a real transcript in Claude Code's shape, with the model
# substituted by this script. Hooks, session state machine and checkpoint
# writer are the real ones.
cat >"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Greet(\"\") returns \"hello \" with a dangling space. Make an empty name greet \"there\" instead."},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:00.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll guard the empty name inside Greet itself rather than at the call sites, so no caller has to repeat the check."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:05.000Z"}
JSONL

hook session-start "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\",\"cwd\":\"$scratch\"}"
hook user-prompt-submit "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"prompt\":\"Make an empty name greet \\\"there\\\".\"}"

cat >"$scratch/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name. An empty name greets "there" rather than
// producing a dangling "hello ", so no caller has to check first.
func Greet(name string) string {
	if name == "" {
		return "hello there"
	}
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
cat >>"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"tu_1","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"$scratch/greet/greet.go","old_string":"return \"hello \" + name","new_string":"if name == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"hello there\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"hello \" + name"}}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:10.000Z"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu_1","content":"The file has been updated."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:11.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The empty-name guard lives inside Greet rather than at each call site, so callers never see a dangling \"hello \"."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:12.000Z"}
JSONL
hook stop "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\"}"

# Commits auto-capture: the post-commit hook entire enable installed writes the
# checkpoint. Never create checkpoints by hand.
machine a "$scratch" sh -c "git add -A && git commit -qm 'fix(greet): greet \"there\" for an empty name'"
hook session-end "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\",\"reason\":\"clear\"}"

[ -n "$(git -C "$scratch" for-each-ref 'refs/entire/checkpoints/' 'refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/')" ] ||
  fail "the commit produced no checkpoint ref"
pass

# -------------------------------------------------------------- leg 3: distill
leg 3

brain_a refresh sessions
# Real extraction over the fixture session; --dry-run would only prove
# planning. Cheap effort keeps the spend at one tiny chunk.
distill_out=$(brain_a distill --branch "$smoke_branch" --effort low --json .)
echo "$distill_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
r = json.load(sys.stdin)
n = r.get("facts_written", r.get("memories_written", r.get("facts", 0)))
if isinstance(n, list):
    n = len(n)
sys.exit(0 if n and int(n) >= 1 else 1)' ||
  { echo "$distill_out" >&2; fail "distill wrote no facts from the fixture session"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 4: recall
leg 4

recall_out=$(brain_a recall "empty name greeting guard" --branch "$smoke_branch" --json)
fact_text=$(echo "$recall_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
facts = json.load(sys.stdin).get("facts") or []
if not facts:
    sys.exit(1)
print(facts[0].get("text") or facts[0].get("content") or "")')
[ -n "$fact_text" ] || { echo "$recall_out" >&2; fail "recall returned no facts on branch $smoke_branch"; }
pass

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 5: graph
leg 5

# --head: the fixture code is committed, and the committed-tree path is the
# cached one agents use by default.
graph_out=$(machine a "$scratch" entire graph query --repo "$scratch" --head --profile full --format json --query "Greet returns a greeting for a name")
echo "$graph_out" | grep -q 'greet\.go' ||
  { echo "$graph_out" | head -c 2000 >&2; fail "graph query did not resolve the Greet fixture symbol"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 6: upload
leg 6

brain_a connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# COR-2233/2234/2235/2236 change the connected-repo sync default (per-fact wire
# in, gitmeta default out). The backend stays EXPLICIT here so this suite is
# valid before and after that lands; revisit the flag value when it does.
brain_a memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (up) failed"

# Remote visibility, straight from the hosted store (endpoint per
# internal/factsync: GET {base}/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts?branch=).
base_url=${API_URL%/api/v1}
needle=$(printf '%s' "$fact_text" | cut -c1-60)
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ENTIRE_TOKEN" \
  "$base_url/api/v1/repos/$REPO_ID/brain/facts?branch=$smoke_branch" |
  json_has_fact "$needle" ||
  fail "the distilled fact is not visible in the hosted store"
pass

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- leg 7: pull
leg 7

git clone -q "$scratch" "$clone_b"
git -C "$clone_b" checkout -q "$smoke_branch"
brain_b connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# Same explicit backend pin as the upload leg (COR-2233 family).
brain_b memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (down) failed"

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu_1","content":"The file has been updated."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:11.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The empty-name guard lives inside Greet rather than at each call site, so callers never see a dangling \"hello \"."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:12.000Z"}
JSONL
hook stop "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\"}"

# Commits auto-capture: the post-commit hook entire enable installed writes the
# checkpoint. Never create checkpoints by hand.
machine a "$scratch" sh -c "git add -A && git commit -qm 'fix(greet): greet \"there\" for an empty name'"
hook session-end "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\",\"reason\":\"clear\"}"

[ -n "$(git -C "$scratch" for-each-ref 'refs/entire/checkpoints/' 'refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/')" ] ||
  fail "the commit produced no checkpoint ref"
pass

# -------------------------------------------------------------- leg 3: distill
leg 3

brain_a refresh sessions
# Real extraction over the fixture session; --dry-run would only prove
# planning. Cheap effort keeps the spend at one tiny chunk.
distill_out=$(brain_a distill --branch "$smoke_branch" --effort low --json .)
echo "$distill_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
r = json.load(sys.stdin)
n = r.get("facts_written", r.get("memories_written", r.get("facts", 0)))
if isinstance(n, list):
    n = len(n)
sys.exit(0 if n and int(n) >= 1 else 1)' ||
  { echo "$distill_out" >&2; fail "distill wrote no facts from the fixture session"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 4: recall
leg 4

recall_out=$(brain_a recall "empty name greeting guard" --branch "$smoke_branch" --json)
fact_text=$(echo "$recall_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
facts = json.load(sys.stdin).get("facts") or []
if not facts:
    sys.exit(1)
print(facts[0].get("text") or facts[0].get("content") or "")')
[ -n "$fact_text" ] || { echo "$recall_out" >&2; fail "recall returned no facts on branch $smoke_branch"; }
pass

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 5: graph
leg 5

# --head: the fixture code is committed, and the committed-tree path is the
# cached one agents use by default.
graph_out=$(machine a "$scratch" entire graph query --repo "$scratch" --head --profile full --format json --query "Greet returns a greeting for a name")
echo "$graph_out" | grep -q 'greet\.go' ||
  { echo "$graph_out" | head -c 2000 >&2; fail "graph query did not resolve the Greet fixture symbol"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 6: upload
leg 6

brain_a connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# COR-2233/2234/2235/2236 change the connected-repo sync default (per-fact wire
# in, gitmeta default out). The backend stays EXPLICIT here so this suite is
# valid before and after that lands; revisit the flag value when it does.
brain_a memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (up) failed"

# Remote visibility, straight from the hosted store (endpoint per
# internal/factsync: GET {base}/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts?branch=).
base_url=${API_URL%/api/v1}
needle=$(printf '%s' "$fact_text" | cut -c1-60)
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ENTIRE_TOKEN" \
  "$base_url/api/v1/repos/$REPO_ID/brain/facts?branch=$smoke_branch" |
  json_has_fact "$needle" ||
  fail "the distilled fact is not visible in the hosted store"
pass

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- leg 7: pull
leg 7

git clone -q "$scratch" "$clone_b"
git -C "$clone_b" checkout -q "$smoke_branch"
brain_b connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# Same explicit backend pin as the upload leg (COR-2233 family).
brain_b memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (down) failed"
brain_b recall "empty name greeting guard" --branch "$smoke_branch" --json |
  json_has_fact "$needle" ||
  fail "the fact pulled on machine B did not merge into its local store"
pass

echo
echo "release:smoke: all 7 legs passed"
