entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

3	import (

9	// distillChildEnvKey carries a replacement child-process environment for the
10	// distill pipeline's agent invocations. It rides the context (like the usage
11	// collector) so the override stays scoped to distill runs: the exec helper is
12	// shared with eval, outline, patterns, skills, and query expansion, whose
13	// latency/quality tradeoffs were never measured.
14	type distillChildEnvKey struct{}
15	
16	// withDistillAgentChildEnv attaches the claude-code child environment to the
17	// distill run's context. Other agents keep the inherited environment: ollama is
18	// HTTP, codex has no equivalent knob, and a --agent-command argv is user-owned.
19	func withDistillAgentChildEnv(ctx context.Context, agent string) context.Context {
20		if agent != "claude-code" {
21			return ctx
22		}
23		return context.WithValue(ctx, distillChildEnvKey{}, distillClaudeChildEnv(os.Environ()))
24	}
25	
26	// distillClaudeChildEnv builds the claude child environment:
27	//
28	//   - MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 disables extended thinking. Measured on a fixed
29	//     20-session corpus (COR-2214): ~97% of extraction output tokens were
30	//     invisible thinking generated at output speed, making API time ~92% of
31	//     each call; disabling it cut the run 7x (545s -> 76s) with fact yield
32	//     intact and the output distribution unchanged beyond run-to-run noise.
33	//     A caller-set MAX_THINKING_TOKENS wins over the default.
34	//   - CLAUDECODE is dropped so distill works when spawned from inside a Claude
35	//     Code session (session-end hook): claude refuses to start nested when it
36	//     is set, and names unsetting it as the supported bypass. The child is a
37	//     headless --print worker with --no-session-persistence, so none of the
38	//     shared-session state the guard protects exists here.
39	//     CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT is dropped with it: only CLAUDECODE gates the
40	//     refusal today (validated against a live session), but this package's own
41	//     detectedAgentHarness reads either as "inside Claude Code", and the child
42	//     is not.
43	func distillClaudeChildEnv(environ []string) []string {
44		out := make([]string, 0, len(environ)+1)
45		hasThinkingBudget := false
46		for _, kv := range environ {
47			if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "CLAUDECODE=") || strings.HasPrefix(kv, "CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=") {
48				continue
49			}
50			if strings.HasPrefix(kv, "MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=") {
51				hasThinkingBudget = true
52			}
53			out = append(out, kv)
54		}
55		if !hasThinkingBudget {
56			out = append(out, "MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0")
57		}
58		return out
59	}

# Backend pinning (COR-2233/2234/2235/2236): the hosted path for a connected
# repo is the per-fact wire, and today `entire brain connect` is the only CLI
# verb that triggers it (hostedFactsSyncAndPull; the others are the session-end
# hook and the watcher). The legacy `memories sync --memories-backend http`
# CAS loop cannot be used here: staging brainstore retired its facts/advance
# endpoint when the per-fact protocol replaced it (404 today). When the
# COR-2233 family exposes an explicit per-fact backend flag on `memories
# sync`, move these two legs onto that flag.
brain_a connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL" ||
  fail "connect (hosted sync up) failed"

# Remote visibility, straight from the hosted store, on this run's unique
# branch (per-fact feed endpoint per internal/factsync/perfact.go:
# GET {base}/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts, paginated).
needle=$(printf '%s' "$fact_text" | cut -c1-60)
remote_has_fact() { # remote_has_fact <branch> <needle>
  python3 - "$API_URL" "$REPO_ID" "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
api, repo, branch, needle = sys.argv[1:5]
token = os.environ["ENTIRE_TOKEN"]
page = ""
for _ in range(100):
    q = {"pageSize": "500"}
    if page:
        q["pageToken"] = page
    url = f"{api}/repos/{repo}/brain/facts?{urllib.parse.urlencode(q)}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    body = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
    for item in body.get("items") or []:
        rec = item.get("record") or {}
        if rec.get("branch") == branch and needle in (rec.get("text") or ""):
            sys.exit(0)
    page = body.get("nextPageToken") or ""
    if not page:
        break
sys.exit(1)
PY
}
remote_has_fact "$smoke_branch" "$needle" ||
  fail "the distilled fact is not visible in the hosted store on branch $smoke_branch"
pass

- **Real bug-shaped gotcha found:** when claude's extraction legitimately returns empty (the distill prompt's default), `claude --print --output-format json` emits `error_during_execution` with no `result`, and distill counts the call as **failed**. The fixture transcript therefore states an explicit decision/invariant with rationale (marked load-bearing in a comment). Possibly worth a ticket — an empty extraction currently looks like an agent failure.
- The staging WAF 403s urllib's default `Python-urllib` user agent; the remote-visibility check sends a custom UA. The script also unsets `CLAUDECODE` (claude's own sanctioned bypass) so the gate can run from inside an agent session.

- Both gotchas are recorded as Brain memories (`project.testing.smoke`), and the working runner coordinates are in my persistent memory for next time.

{"id":"COR-2233","title":"Stable release: one memory-sync path — per-fact wire everywhere, retire CAS and the gitmeta default","description":"Decision (evis, 2026-10-22, stable-release scoping): the per-fact wire (<issue id="1adb7ab6-393d-4506-be10-44c6e0763800" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2126/entire-brain-plugin-per-fact-push-reachability-filtered-pull-replaces">COR-2126</issue>, `factsync/perfact.go`) is the long-term memory-sync path. Manual and background sync must use the same wire before the stable CLI release, because every shipped default joins the backwards-compat surface.

This reverses the <issue id="65bf55d0-55c2-4788-b068-aacd8515875f" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2211/decide-should-plain-memories-sync-use-the-hosted-backend-on-a">COR-2211</issue> outcome (keep local-gitmeta default, document it). Reconciliation with ADR-P1-A no-implicit-egress: connecting a repo is the consent; a hosted default applies only on connected repos.

Current state:

* `memories sync` on a connected repo defaults to local-gitmeta; hosted sync needs `--memories-backend=http`.
* Manual `--memories-backend=http` drives the branch-head CAS wire (`factsync.HTTPServer`, `/brain/facts` + `/brain/facts/advance`, proposals queue). Connected background sync (`hostedFactsSyncAndPull`) drives the per-fact upsert/delta-feed wire. Two hosted wires that can diverge.

Scope (sub-issues):

1. Connected repos: plain `memories sync` uses the hosted per-fact wire by default.
2. Retire the CAS branch-head wire for manual sync; per-fact is the only hosted path.
3. Retire local-gitmeta as a default and sweep flags/help/docs. Open decision inside: gitmeta is the only memory-sharing path for repos not connected to brainstore (git metadata refs, no egress). Either keep it as an explicit opt-in for unconnected repos or remove it and accept that unconnected repos have local-only memories.

Compat requirements:

* Existing `--memories-backend` values keep working through the stable release: removed values fail with a clear message or map to the new behavior with a one-time deprecation warning (precedent: `ENTIRE_BRAIN_ALLOW_HOSTED`, PR #390).
* `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` / `LOCAL_ONLY` still suppress all hosted sync regardless of defaults.

Done means: one hosted wire in the codebase, one documented default, help text and docs match behavior, and the stable-release checklist item "hosted sync surface frozen" can be checked off.","status":"In Progress","assignee":null}

Decision required first (evis): gitmeta is currently the only memory-sharing path for repos NOT connected to brainstore (git metadata refs, no egress). Options:

1. Remove gitmeta entirely — unconnected repos have local-only memories; sharing requires connecting.
2. Keep gitmeta as explicit opt-in (`--memories-backend=gitmeta`) for unconnected repos, no default anywhere.

Then:

* Sweep every CLI surface that mentions backends: flags, help text, status/setup output, docs (reference, operations, getting-started), MCP tool descriptions.

* One consistent story: a user reading `memories sync --help` learns the default, the alternatives, and what connectedness changes.","status":"Backlog","assignee":null}

One-shot blast radius for changing a symbol

Usage:
  entire graph impact --symbol NAME|<file>:<line> --repo . [--depth 1|2] [--limit 15] [--format text|json]

Everything the graph knows about changing one symbol in a single bounded explanation: direct + transitive callers (depth <=2), callees, type consumers (USES_TYPE/PARAM_TYPE/RETURNS_TYPE), data flows, files that historically co-change with the symbol's file, and same-container siblings. Run this before changing a function/type's behavior.

Ambiguous names return the definition list; rerun with --file/--line/--kind (or --symbol <file>:<line>) to pick one.

  --symbol NAME|<file>:<line>

Here's where this stands and what's next. (The sibling workspace already owns most of it — COR-2234 and COR-2235 are In Review; COR-2236 is Backlog waiting on you.)

## What "retire CAS locally" removes in this repo

The non-test consumers of the CAS machinery are exactly two commands, confirmed by graph impact + text sweep:

| Surface | Code | Fate |
|---|---|---|
| `memories sync` CAS loop | `internal/cli/facts_sync_cmd.go` (635 lines) + `factsync/sync.go` read-merge-CAS over the Store interface | replaced by per-fact (`hostedFactsSyncAndPull` path) |
| CAS set-head client | `Current`/`CurrentWithAuthors`/`Advance` in `factsync/httpserver.go` | delete — staging already 404s `facts/advance` |
| Proposals queue | `factsync/httpproposals.go` + `proposal_repair.go` + `memories proposals` (`facts_proposals_cmd.go`, 430 lines) | dies with CAS; only the CAS wire ever used it |
| local-gitmeta store | bare repo under `<cache>/brain/<key>/gitmeta.git`, built in `facts_sync_cmd.go` | the COR-2236 decision |

That's ~1,900 lines plus their tests, and the per-fact wire (`perfact.go`) is untouched by the removal.

## What's actually next, in order

1. **Your decision on COR-2236** — gitmeta's fate for unconnected repos. If you're retiring CAS locally "as well," option 1 (remove gitmeta entirely; unconnected repos are local-only, sharing = connect) is the only consistent choice: keeping gitmeta as opt-in means keeping the entire CAS merge loop alive for one niche path, which defeats "one sync path in the codebase." The compat item that needs an answer either way: already-synced `gitmeta.git` refs must not break — probably a one-time read/import path rather than live support.
2. **Land COR-2234/2235** (in review). Two checklist items from 2235 still need explicit confirmation: whether prod brainstore keeps the CAS endpoints for a deprecation window, and the `docs/proposal-queue-repair.md` operational dependency before deleting the proposals code. `memories proposals` disappearing is user-visible — release notes.
3. **Backend-flag compat sweep** — removed `--memories-backend` values fail clearly or map with a one-time deprecation warning (PR #390 precedent), help/docs/MCP descriptions say one consistent story.
4. **This workspace (the gate):** `release:smoke` passes unchanged through all of this because it deliberately never touches the CAS path — legs 6/7 pin on `connect`'s per-fact sync. Once 2234/2235 merge, the follow-up here is small: re-run the smoke against the new RC SHA, and switch legs 6/7 to plain `memories sync` (which then *is* the per-fact wire on connected repos) so the gate exercises the shipped verb instead of piggybacking on connect. The script comment already marks exactly that spot.

Decision (evis, 2026-10-22): **option 1 — remove gitmeta entirely.** Unconnected repos have local-only memories; sharing requires `entire brain connect`. Keeping gitmeta as an opt-in would keep the whole read-merge-CAS loop alive for one niche path, which defeats COR-2233's "one sync path".

Consequences being implemented (stacked on PR #452 / `per-fact-wire-memory-sync`):

- `memories sync` on an unconnected repo exits with a clear message: memories stay local, `entire brain connect` is how you share. On a connected repo it is the per-fact wire (PR #452 behavior).
- The factsync CAS seam (`factsync/sync.go` read-merge-CAS loop) and the gitmeta bare store under the brain cache are deleted; PR #452 already left gitmeta as the seam's only implementor.
- `--memories-backend` compat per the PR #390 precedent: `http` maps to the per-fact wire with a one-time deprecation note; `local-gitmeta` fails with a message naming the decision and the connect path.
- Already-synced `gitmeta.git` stores live under the plugin cache; they are left on disk and ignored (cache data, reconstructible). Branch memory stores in the data dir are untouched — nothing a user distilled or authored is lost.

entries.name: mcp__linear__save_comment
entries.description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead).

id.description: Comment ID. If provided, updates the existing comment

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

parentId.description: Parent comment ID (for replies, only when creating)

body.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

entries.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue
